name: C'est La Vie
beta: Reach a flake via a shallow corner, then step rightward onto it and layback its left-facing edge to a notch, which you surmount. From there either work up a tricky slab left to a two-bolt anchor, or follow the slab and arete straight up to a higher anchor. Most parties stop after this pitch and rappel.
overview: A popular two-pitch line low and right on Redgarden's south face. The 5.9 first pitch, liebacking a big flake through a notch onto a slab, is often done alone; the second pitch climbs thin face in the dihedral above.

current.area_walk_in: Head north past the Whale's Tail on its western flank, then scramble a short distance east into the rocky gully that separates it from the big wall.
current.descent: rap 150 ft with two ropes
current.location: From a broken ledge under a huge right-angling dihedral, low and right on Redgarden's southern side, roughly in line with the concrete pad by the Whale's Tail

name: Calypso
beta:
Either squirm up the slot behind the boulder at the base or, preferably, come across from the leftward side to the large dihedral that faces right. The corner ends at a roof; lieback rightward over it to a ledge, then step down to the belay at two bolts.

Pitch two follows a short thin crack leftward and easier rock; pitch three swings rightward to a corner before heading left to the top.
overview: One of the canyon's busiest moderates: a big right-facing dihedral to a roof and a bolted belay, a short thin crack, then a corner to Wind Tower's summit.

current.area_walk_in: Step across the plank footbridge spanning South Boulder Creek. A path leads eastward under the south face; a separate path ascends rightward from the bridge to the west face.
current.descent: scramble northeast down ledgy slabs into a notch, rappel a short way on one rope from 2 bolts (or downclimb 5.4), then descend the gully west of the tower
current.anchor: bolted belay after the first pitch
current.location: Directly left of an enormous block at the foot of the tower's west side

name: Candyman
beta: A short, steep pitch up a wall of sandy pockets that ends at a two-bolt station; a few pitons are already in place along the way.
overview: Short pitch on sandy pockets up steep rock to a bolted station.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: inside the deep slot on the Drug Wall's eastern side

name: Captain Cod Piece
beta: Tucked immediately behind a cluster of large firs, the route is a slim finger-width fissure. Bring small wires and TCUs.
overview: A steep, sustained thin-finger jam crack hidden behind large firs; stays shady.

current.descent: walk west along ledges to get down
current.location: Behind a stand of big fir trees at the base of the wall

name: Euphoria
beta: Clip three bolts, then bend up-left into the slender crack of the adjacent route and lower from its anchor.
overview: Bolted start on the face beside its neighbour, which then slants up and left to join the neighbour's thin crack for the finish.

current.descent: lower off
current.location: beside Phaedra, on its right

name: Chain of Command
beta: Reach the foot of a hanging dihedral by climbing the face diagonally leftward; the 5.9 moves here feel scary. Then climb the corner to two bolts. This opening pitch doubles as a separate route.
overview: Climbs Bonzo's corner, then moves left onto the edge of Turnkorner Buttress for bolted face climbing on flakes, with a short, harder final pitch. Pitches two and three can be linked.

current.area_walk_in: Walk the Black Canyon trail westward, passing under the entire west side of Lumpy Ridge, for two stiff miles. A little cairn flags the spur path, which winds up the steep forested hillside under the buttress and finishes close to an enormous flake propped against Turnkorner Buttress.
current.descent: Rap the line; one rope works but a 60 m is better. Or continue to the saddle
current.location: Begins up Bonzo, below the hanging dihedral about 120 ft left of Turnkorner

name: Cheops
beta: Eight bolts lead directly along the rounded arete to the ledge above; watch for slightly flaky rock in the upper part.
overview: A good bolted line up a blunt arete beside the prominent dihedral, finishing on a ledge with a two-bolt belay. The rock turns somewhat flaky near the top.

current.area_walk_in: A faint path heads into the valley toward the south, fords the stream, then climbs loose gravel to the foot of the rock. For Sphinx Crack, continue up onto the ledge along the east side.
current.descent: rap or lower 80 ft
current.location: reached by crossing the big broken ledge beneath the major crack, near where the dihedral line ends midway up

name: Cleft Palate
beta: Pitch one crosses an easy slab with no protection to a slender, curving crack, which you follow rightward before crossing beneath the arch toward a belay stance. The second pitch hand-traverses and face climbs along the arch, with a single 5.11a spot, to easier ground.
overview: A slab to a curving thin crack, then a long horizontal traverse beneath the right-slanting arch on Crescent Wall’s western half.

current.location: Toward the wall’s left end, nearly straight below where the right-slanting arch begins, left of a big pine

name: Climb of the Ancient Mariner
beta: Share the opening 50 feet of the neighbouring route, then leave it once you reach the alcove, heading left into a corner that faces right. Ascend until the roof blocks you and go around its left end with a bolt for protection, then finish up the slab, clipping a pair of additional bolts, to the anchor.
overview: Popular Bookend line up clean slab next to Sorcerer: a corner, a bolt-protected roof, then bolted slab climbing, finishing on Sorcerer.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the Lumpy Ridge trail west past the old Twin Owls area, continue beyond the Book and the Bookmark, then take a faint spur to the southeast prow. A little scrambling is needed to get to the routes on the right.
current.location: Shares the first ~50 ft of Sorcerer, then branches left at the alcove into a corner facing right

name: Cocaine
beta: A wandering slab where every difficult section is well protected. To tame rope drag, put a long sling on the traverse bolt found about midway through the first pitch.
overview: Superb slab climb winding upward for two long pitches, topping out on the pointed east summit; most parties do only the first pitch. The hard moves are well protected.

current.descent: after pitch 1, downclimb a gully or rappel

name: Cold Frize
beta: Climb the obvious open corner and get past the roof by its right-hand end, ending at the neighbouring route's anchors. A small rack complements the few bolts present.
overview: Follows an evident open corner, then exits around the right end of a roof to finish at the anchors of a neighbouring route. A couple of bolts protect the line.

current.area_walk_in: Roughly ten minutes of walking. Climb a brief gully beneath the face, slip through a notch, then descend eastward along the foot of the south face through scrub oak to a crude trail over the boulder field under the smooth slab.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: open corner, going round the roof to its right

name: Confines of Power
beta: Seven bolts lead straight upward to a permanent anchor that sits a bit right of the neighbouring route.
overview: A standout seven-bolt sport pitch on the north side of The Thumb.

current.area_walk_in: A signed trail leaves the Peak View Drive lot and climbs about three-quarters of a mile, gaining roughly 400 feet, to reach the Needle and then the Thumb a little farther uphill.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: North side of The Thumb, just right of the neighboring line; Vapor Trail shares its lower part

name: Core Dump
beta: Hard slab moves right off the ground, protected by four bolts, lead to an easy crack with a stance for belaying. From there, cracks continue to the top of the formation.
overview: Hard slab moves on four bolts start from the ground, leading into an easy crack, then to a stance for belaying. More crack climbing continues up to the summit.

current.area_walk_in: A short walk from the road to the base; the wall rises straight up on the north side.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Corner Pump Station
beta:
Begin by climbing a neighbouring route, then hand-traverse rightward to an alcove where nuts and a piton are fixed. Above, lieback two overhanging cracks beside a fixed blade; that stretch is the 11b crux.

Next comes a lieback and finger crack curving out left. Some 25 feet along it becomes an undercling at 11a, then a brief 5.9 corner ends at a stance under two corners facing left.
overview: A free version of an old aid pitch: hand traverse to an alcove, then pumping lieback cracks high in the Book's central corner, on its right-hand face.

current.area_walk_in: From the trailhead, hike west past the Twin Owls formation and follow the Black Canyon Trail to The Book, adding roughly another two-thirds of a mile beyond Twin Owls. Scramble up to the base of the Pages Wall.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Starts about 125 ft up, at the belay on a jammed flake, reached by Howling at the Wind's first pitch or by El Camino Real

name: Country Club Crack
beta: The first pitch opens with a boulder problem on polished holds past two bolts, the route's crux. After that, work a clumsy hand-sized crack up to a belay perch called The Bar, with a lot of air beneath it.
overview: A must-do line of unrelenting upright and leaning cracks. The first pitch opens with a bolted boulder problem on polished holds, then a clumsy hand jam up to an airy ledge; the second pitch goes through a roof into a steep finger seam.

current.area_walk_in: The base of the formation is a short flat step from the roadside pullout; the ground at the foot is uneven.
current.location: Begins immediately beside Athlete's Feat, on its right.

name: Coyote
beta: The first pitch follows excellent stone on the arete's right-hand side, with five bolts and the hardest moves saved for the upper part.
overview: A bolted arete on the West Owl beside the Silly Putty corner, with excellent rock and its hardest moves near the first anchor; most parties lower from there.

current.area_walk_in: Take the trail toward Gem Lake, and just beyond the first aspens turn onto a spur that doubles back leftward and ascends the hillside under the Lower Owls' western face. The spur keeps rising up a gully until it meets the Roosting Ramp's far western tip.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Crack of Fear
beta:
Begin low on the ramp, beneath the big offwidth. Jam up the left side of the small pillar called the Rat's Tooth and squeeze to a piton, then step out leftward onto a flake for the belay. The next pitch wrestles through a slot of ten inches, then undercuts leftward to a stance.

Further body-jamming, easier at 5.10a, reaches a gentle ramp, and the top is easy in either direction. Carry big-bro or tubular chocks along with a light rack topping out at a #4 Camalot.
overview: Colorado's best-known offwidth: about 250 ft of crack that stays 5 inches or wider up the East Owl, strenuous and relentless from the Rat's Tooth to the final ramp.

current.area_walk_in: Take the trail toward Gem Lake, and just beyond the first aspens turn onto a spur that doubles back leftward and ascends the hillside under the Lower Owls' western face. The spur keeps rising up a gully until it meets the Roosting Ramp's far western tip.
current.descent: Many teams lower from anchors about 75 ft up, below the crux; otherwise finish to the summit and use the saddle descent
current.location: Roosting Ramp base, under the huge offwidth; begins beside the small pillar called the Rat's Tooth

name: Synchronicity
beta: Climb the steep slab to the right of a neighbouring route, face-climbing through thin, fractured crack systems and clipping three bolts. Rappel from the anchors to the right.
overview: Face climbing on a steep slab, following slender fractured seams and clipping three bolts.

current.area_walk_in: Find the climbers' trail through the forest and up the steep talus slope, heading for the canyon just right of the main wall. Loose rock is common, so avoid kicking stones down onto others.
current.descent: rappel from anchors off to the right
current.location: steep slab beside Where Eagles Dare, on its right

name: Crescent Arch
beta: Follow the huge dihedral that leans and arches leftward on the southern wall's right-hand edge. The crack calls for gear as big as six inches.
overview: A strenuous wide-crack classic up the huge arching corner at the right end of Crescent Wall.

current.descent: two-rope rap from the arch top, or continue up Strategic Arms
current.location: The big left-facing corner that arcs leftward at the wall’s right end

name: Politics of Scarcity
beta: Jam the slender crack that lies between two adjacent routes. Protection is minimal: a single bolt and an epoxied placement.
overview: A tips-sized crack squeezed between two neighbouring routes, rated R because it is so thinly protected.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Poultry in Motion
beta: Edge up the outside of the arch along a line of seven bolts to the arch belay. The route wanders over steep wall to the arch's right.
overview: A steep face route up the wall beside the large arch, clipping bolts along the way.

current.descent: rappel on a double rope from the anchors crowning the arch
current.location: starts the same way as Crescent Arch

name: Strategic Arms
beta:
Get to the rappel stance via one of the three routes immediately beside it. Beyond the anchor, trend rightward at 11d to a sling belay where the roof ends, then climb a trough at 11a to a comfortable ledge.

Raise your belay leftward beyond a big tree (now fallen), and finish up the face above at 11a to the wall's top. Protection on these upper pitches is poor.
overview: Reached by climbing one of two neighbouring routes to the upper ledge. Three short face leads then trend up and right: bolts to the arch ledge, thin face to a groove and a tree ledge, then a steep, largely unprotected wall with a pair of overlaps before the top.

name: Cryogenics
beta:
Pitch one follows a pale, steep dihedral under a prominent corner, laybacking and jamming a thin crack of finger and hand size, with 5.9+ moves close to the top, to a big ledge with anchors.

Rappel there, or do the shorter second pitch, which swings left beneath the steep headwall before returning right above it. Take a rack of cams and bigger nuts.
overview: Arguably the finest crack on Independence Pass: layback and jam a thin hand-to-finger crack in a steep white corner to a big ledge. Most rappel there; a shorter second pitch skirts the headwall on the left.

current.descent: rappel from the first-pitch ledge
current.anchor: fixed anchors on a large ledge atop pitch 1
current.location: just left of where the central buttress meets the ground, beneath a striking white corner

name: Curving Crack
beta: Open by laybacking or jamming a crack set in a corner. Next, stem and layback the corner as it sweeps leftward up to a roof, and finish with a crack above it that leads to a two-bolt anchor.
overview: A corner crack that can be laybacked or jammed, then a corner that bends leftward up to a roof, and a final crack to the anchor.

current.area_walk_in: The base of the formation is a short flat step from the roadside pullout; the ground at the foot is uneven.
current.descent: rappel
current.location: Found on the next buttress to the northwest, past Final Exam.

name: Dags in Beanland
beta:
Launch from the lowest slab, close to the rock's centre, angling rightward past one bolt to a roomy ledge. The next lead begins with a brief crack beside the belay, then a lovely slab with four bolts, a small roof, and another bolt, and a two-bolt stance to finish the lead.

Above, go straight to a bolt and trace the rosy dike that bends across the slab to a little ledge. A short pitch gains a big shelf with a juniper, and a final slab with two bolts and a trough leads close to the summit, where a scramble finishes it.
overview: The best line on this low-angle slab: several pitches of bolt-and-gear friction, a small roof on the second pitch, and a pink dike higher up.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: at the lowest point of the slab, near its middle

name: Dead Boy
beta: Follow the good crack in the stepped corner that faces left over roughly 90 feet, then make a tricky traverse rightward to join a neighbouring route. Carry cams to #2 plus extra stoppers.
overview: About 90 ft of good crack in a stepped corner, then a hard traverse right into Living Dead.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the usual trail toward the Book, then bear left at the foot of the Pages Wall and pass the vertical cracks; the first cleft on the right leads up to the buttress.
current.descent: Rappel about 70 ft from Living Dead's first belay, or carry on up that route
current.location: Stepped corner (facing left) below and right of Flaked Out, immediately left of Living Dead

name: Dead in Bed
beta:
Pitch one scales the buttress on a chain of flakes, with a committing move onto a jug, then trends up-left to a diagonal-crack belay. Pitch two works across to a bolt on a neighbouring route, then up-right to a big boulder-strewn ledge.

Pitch three begins on a different route but follows a crack leftward and round into a dihedral, then a fist crack of about 15 feet joins another route for the run to the summit.
overview: Three pitches up the west buttress: flakes and a bold reach to a jug, a traverse past the Fantasy Ridge bolt to a bouldery ledge, then a corner and fist crack joining Sidewinder.

current.location: Immediately right of the big square-cut chimney on the west side

name: Death by Drowning
beta:
Three pitches. Start with a short, easy lead beside a flake up to a little pine for the belay. The bolted second pitch trends rightward to a band of quartz, then continues up steep face moves (roughly 5.10+) before bolts mark a belay on a gentler slab.

Finish by surmounting the arch overhead, around 5.8, then belay among the water-carved pockets known as tinajas.
overview: Three pitches on Arch Rock: an easy start beside Hollow Flake, a bolted, steep face pitch along a quartz dike, then over the arch to water-worn potholes.

current.area_walk_in: Several short, steep trails climb the slope to the base of the crag.
current.location: Starts beside Hollow Flake, climbing its right edge to a little pine

name: Delusions of Grandeur
beta: Clip the line of bolts up and out through the overhang, then settle into the technical face moves above.
overview: A bolted line that leaves the ground through an overhang and ends on technical face climbing, standing well left of a neighbouring route. Described as excellent.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: bolt line crossing an overhang, roughly a hundred feet to the left from The Terror

name: Dementia
beta:
Roughly twenty feet off the ground a tricky lieback gives entry to a brief hand crack and then the main dihedral. Stem, bridge and rely on footwork up the dihedral, with decent gear along the way, until a step left onto an airy foothold.

Finish by squirming up a hand-crack slot, and watch for loose blocks lying on top.
overview: Rated the best line on the crag: cracks lead into a narrow V-shaped corner jammed on fingers, then more cracks to bolts.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: The crack immediately to the right of the Last Call line

name: Desdichado
beta: Use the opening pitch of C'est la Vie, carry on through its crux, then swing out over the badly overhanging upper wall clipping 4 bolts. Pull over the lip of the roof and belay from 3 bolts just above.
overview: An extreme bolted extension above C'est La Vie that powers out a steeply overhanging headwall and pulls a roof lip to a bolted stance.

current.area_walk_in: Head north past the Whale's Tail on its western flank, then scramble a short distance east into the rocky gully that separates it from the big wall.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Desolation Angels
beta: Start by scaling a ramp, then shuffle left to the foot of the dihedral. Climb the dihedral itself and go over the roof capping it, where the crux comes.
overview: A dihedral-and-roof line in red rock at the far left side of an amphitheater, the leftmost route of the formation. It finishes through a conspicuous square roof.

current.descent: rappel from a big tree just west of the route with two ropes
current.location: the farthest-left line here, following a reddish dihedral then a boxy roof at the left of the amphitheater

name: Diagonal Finger Crack
beta: Jam the slanting finger crack immediately east of the Green line all the way up; an old bolt sits at the top.
overview: A short slanting finger crack on Green Thumb, the next line right of Green Crack, with an aged bolt up top and a tree rappel close by.

current.descent: rap off the lesser of a pair of trees just south
current.anchor: tree (smaller of two, a few yards south)
current.location: the slanting finger crack next to Green Crack, on its right

name: Diesel and Dust
beta: The first lead is excellent face work using flakes and small edges, finishing at a semi-hanging stance. The second heads directly up steep, rough stone to a two-bolt belay.
overview: Two-pitch face line using flakes and small edges; pitch 1 ends at a semi-hanging stance and pitch 2 heads directly up steep, brittle rock.

current.area_walk_in: Walk uphill on the established trails toward the face; the long dihedral on the face makes an easy landmark to aim for.
current.descent: rappel the line, or scramble down the south side

name: Direct Hit
beta:
The first pitch climbs vertical rock rightward out of the gully with little gear, reaching a small stance. The second pitch follows an easy crack to the slabs near the summit.

Bring RPs, wired nuts and TCUs for the protection, and walk down toward the west.
overview: A superb two-pitch face climb that begins near the head of the gully, along the face's western flank. The first lead is the serious one, on vertical rock with sparse protection, while the second is much easier.

current.area_walk_in: For the south face, head west from the saddle on a brief path that leads to the cliff foot. The north face is reached separately.
current.descent: walk off west
current.location: high in the gully at the west edge of the face

name: Direct North Face
beta:
The first pitch goes via flakes beneath a corner, then a second brief corner past a bolt. Move left to a sloping stance, then smear leftward below a little roof, then go right to a shallow corner and a two-bolt shelf.

The second pitch layback leftward beside fixed pins with a committing mantle up to a narrow ledge, with easier terrain leading above.
overview: A steep and spectacular direct climb of the north face that links several established lines. Expect sustained climbing in the 5.10 range, one move of 5.11 plus awkward gear.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Divination
beta:
Start roughly thirty feet along the ramp and clip eleven bolts on the black wall to a narrow ledge. Next, trace a dihedral system rightward until it fades, crank to the arete, and follow a sharply rising ramp to a belay.

The third pitch climbs a black ramp, works left under a roof, then goes straight to a ledge with an anchor.
overview: A long, bolt-protected line up the black west face of the crag, three pitches of sustained wall and ramp climbing. It begins on an extensive wooded ramp rising beside the stream.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the obvious trail south from the lot, then drop around the formation through a notch and down a gully. If the ground begins to feel like fifth class, you have gone too far.
current.location: up the forested ramp below the west face, a short way above its foot

name: Don't Stop Now
beta: Follow the shallow corner up the far right of the face; the lone bolt is about midway up.
overview: A short face climb that follows a shallow corner on the right-hand portion of the face, protected by a single bolt.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Doric Dihedral
beta: Find the prominent dihedral and climb it. Continually awkward, the route is said to be cruxed by a mantel up high in the dihedral, where the gear is scary.
overview: A hard dihedral on Ridge Two (Satan's Slab), freed in the 1980s.

current.area_walk_in: Walk the NCAR trail west about half a mile to its junction with the Mesa trail, then north a short way over Skunk Creek. A faint path heads west up Skunk Canyon beneath the big-roofed slab of Ridge One; the following rib on your right is Satan's Slab.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Dr. Gizmo
beta:
The first pitch is the easy opening lead of the neighbouring dihedral route, up to a belay. The second jams cracks that widen from fingers to hands, just left of a dark streak, ending at a stance under a small tree.

On the last pitch, angle rightward and upward below a little roof, pull around it on its left, and continue over easier broken ground. Retreat is by rappel with two ropes.
overview: A superb three-pitch crack climb on the steep, streaked face beside Undecided, first freed in 1980.

current.descent: rappel the route with two ropes
current.location: The steep, streaked face to the right of the Undecided dihedral; starts up Undecided's first pitch
